concern_results.conclusion: I checked six areas against the diff and found no code failure path in any of them. (1) GIT_* scrub parity: review_diff.py and review_diff_clients.py define identical 23-key, 7-key and 2-prefix lists, and every changed git or child-CLI call site in the diff now passes git_environment() (Git.raw/out, private_opencode_root init, Codex, Claude, OpenCode, Kimi). The 10c2 test checks binding via a head assertion and checks each child environment. (2) Caching boundary: Candidate.bind passes head and untracked only to the first digest(). The changed() path still calls an uncached digest(), and 10f and 10f1b guard it. (3) check-size-budget.sh: porcelain -z --no-renames entries are parsed with byteslice(3..), which is correct for the XY<space>path format. The CR-only base count now uses ref_info_for_text through head_ref_infos (reused when the SHA-1 matches) or base blobs, a missing blob degrades to reference_line_trend_partial, and g10b pins parity. (4) paired-eval cleanup: it only runs when interrupted, no init event was seen, and a cwd was given, and it is scoped to the sample's own project slug. (5) Obligation preservation: the 102 rows are claims the packet cannot verify mechanically. (6) Item-9 gate-fireability: no changed gate in the diff can be reached while skipping its trigger. One evidence inconsistency is reported as a finding.

The containment evidence for the shared-gate change holds within the diff. No exemptions were added. The new base census fails closed to unknown rather than reporting a pass. The hygiene gate gains the two new targets. Security review is explicitly recorded as pending-dedicated-review, not marked passed. The one remaining gap is inconsistent mutation-count claims across carriers (P2).
